description.from:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a editor, I want all relevant publication and Section matches retained, so that one discovery can inform several editorial outputs.

Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet):
```gherkin
Feature: Preserve multiple Cyclotron matches for monitored material
  Scenario: Material matches multiple outputs
    Given a canonical candidate is discovered by one Monitor
    When authorized publication and Section classifiers evaluate it
    Then all applicable matches and their decision provenance may be retained
    And a sponsoring desk or section-selector suggestion does not erase other Section-fit outputs
    And editorial ownership, conflicting coverage and placement remain explicit later decisions
  Scenario: Preserve review boundaries
    Given a Monitor or Cyclotron proposes a candidate match
    When its output is recorded
    Then the prediction alone does not make the Reference accepted evidence or a human training label
```

Relates to PPY-b0396f and current shared-site Cyclotron PPY-0a285b. Do not duplicate/reconfigure engines per Monitor. Cross-publication consumers require explicit publication scope and permitted sharing design. This future vision does not silently change the existing single chosen-Section training contract.

Relates to PPY-b0396f and current shared-site Cyclotron PPY-0a285b. Do not duplicate/reconfigure engines per Monitor. Latest priority and initial consumers: inbound Monitoring is Ryan's highest near-term value, independent of Markus for everything, outbound RSS/Atom and headless delivery. Initial consumers are the academic Papyrus publication, Threat Intelligence AND Anth.us, configured through the same publication-agnostic Papyrus capability rather than special implementations. Morning relevant discoveries must reach the actual configured Cyclotron classifiers with attributable classification evidence; a manual research list alone is not completion. No automatic human labels. No blocking dependency on the Markus initiative, outgoing feeds, authored-page migration or email-monitor implementation is introduced.

First small vertical slice: validate and configure 3–5 real sources across those consumers, prioritizing Hacker News, arXiv AI papers, the current Hugging Face paper offering, security/privacy publications and CVE/advisory sources. Final source/publication bindings are verified, not inferred. Cadence is configurable around 15 minutes where source limits and update frequency permit, with checkpoints, deduplication, new/updated-item handling, provenance and visible retryable failures. The desired “tonight or tomorrow” urgency expresses value, not permission to deploy or start coding.

Source validation evidence from this planning pass: https://huggingface.co/papers currently identifies Daily Papers (daily/weekly/monthly views) and offers email subscription; no official RSS feed, stable API contract or Papers With Code successor status was established. Validate an allowed feed/API/crawler method before selecting it. Official arXiv RSS/Atom documentation https://info.arxiv.org/help/rss.html describes subject feeds and daily updates; its cadence need not be 15 minutes. Review current source terms/rate/access requirements before implementation. HN candidates remain https://news.ycombinator.com/rss and https://github.com/HackerNews/API . No subscriptions, mailbox connections, model calls or paid access in this task.

Near-term pilot task: PPY-3212f123-2cc6-4464-b3b6-1c32bfbdda25. End-to-end recurring/classification behavior: PPY-b8b15cfc-f06e-4f19-9574-00c3c233d56c.
